name: mouse_lidar
agent_report:
Video shows a Logitech MX Master-style wireless mouse sitting stationary on a wooden desk while the camera orbits ~329 deg around it. No button press, wheel roll or other articulation is operated; the mouse is rigid for the whole 20.3 s.

Model:
- floor: static wooden table plane from RGB-D.
- base: mouse approximated as single static box, visual-hull envelope from 48 views / 43871 voxels over 1217/1217 frames.
- Size: 121.3 x 75.2 x 54.7 mm, top 56 mm above floor from depth. Consistent with MX Master ~125x84x51 mm; concave dents / side scoops facing no camera are filled by convex hull, as expected for fit_static.
- No joints: 0-DoF rigid object on table. Replay covers 73-99% of mask, typically ~85-95%, staying on the mouse body through the orbit.
- Physics: base plastic, 0.14 kg, friction 0.5. 0.353 l solid -> ~397 kg/m3 bulk density, plausible for hollow plastic shell + electronics/battery.

Limitation: buttons, main scroll wheel and thumb wheel are real micro-joints but never actuated in this video and too small for depth to resolve. Model treats mouse as one rigid body. To capture clicks/wheels, reshoot close-up top-down with finger operating each control.

design.object: ergonomic wireless computer mouse - Logitech MX Master style

parts.base: complete mouse body with palm hump, front click nose, thumb-rest wing, main metal scroll wheel, mode button and side thumb wheel

assumptions: Front (+X, narrow nose with scroll wheel) vs rear (-X, high palm) orientation inferred from video and top-view silhouette; mirror in Y would be equivalent.
Underside assumed flat sitting on table at z=-27.5 to close measured bottom; underside detail not seen.
Rounded corner radii (15/10/6/5mm) estimated from video to get blobby ergonomic look.
Main scroll wheel slot and click split lines not modeled as geometry; wheel shown protruding above top surface.
Thumb pad shown as thin rubber inset on side of thumb wing; texture not modeled.
Colours for dark slate body and silver metal wheels sampled from video frames.
design.notes: Single static link fills measured bbox X[-65,65] Y[-40,40.5] Z[-27.5,28.5] vs measured [-64.4,64.5] [-40.7,41.5] [-27.6,27.7], matching length 129mm of MX Master.

design.object: ergonomic wireless computer mouse - Logitech MX Master style

parts.base: complete mouse body with high rear palm hump, narrower front click nose, side thumb-rest wing, main metal scroll wheel, manual-shift button and side thumb wheel

assumptions: Front is +X narrow nose with main scroll wheel, rear is -X high palm; orientation inferred from video.
Top silhouette tapers from wide rear to narrower front, so rear is made wider than front with large corner radii to avoid boxy rectangular projection.
Underside assumed flat at z=-27 to close measured bottom; underside detail not seen.
Corner radii 21/15/7/8 estimated from video to get domed ergonomic look.
Dark slate body and silver metal wheels sampled from video; thumb pad darker rubber.
design.notes: Fits measured bbox X[-65,64] Y[-41.5,41] Z[-27,27] vs measured [-64.4,64.5] [-40.7,41.5] [-27.6,27.7]. Two overlapping rounded volumes replace single boxy slab to give curved dome and tapered top view.

design.note: Visual geometry designed by the model from the measured extents; collision, joints and physics are the measured ones.

measurement_source.note: Depth is measured by the capture device and can contain noise and drift; hidden dimensions may be assumed by the shape builder.

alignment.method: bounded rigid ICP to observed depth; no scale change

warnings: The static model is an approximate shape based on observed depth; hidden surfaces and complete dimensions are not measured.
base: SAM 3D passed geometric checks, but texture and hidden surfaces were not validated; inspect the visual from multiple views.
Physics properties were estimated from video, not independently measured.
quality.note: Coverage uses SAM masks, not independent ground truth. Passing basic checks does not prove accuracy.
